content: This medication is used to treat constipation by increasing the bulk of stool, which helps stimulate bowel movements. It is classified as a bulk-forming laxative and is not absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract. To use this medication, take it orally as directed by your doctor. If you are self-treating, follow the instructions on the product packaging. For tablets or caplets, take up to two at a time, up to six times daily, but do not exceed 12 caplets in a day. Each dose must be followed by a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters). If the mixture becomes too thick, you may add more liquid. Dosage depends on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. It is important to take this medication with sufficient liquid to prevent it from swelling in the throat, which could cause choking. Do not take this product if you have difficulty swallowing. If you experience chest pain, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, or breathing after taking this product, seek immediate medical attention. This product may take 1 to 3 days to start working. Use it regularly for the best results, and try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If your condition persists, worsens, or if you experience rectal bleeding, consult your doctor promptly. Common side effects may include gas or stomach cramping. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms of an allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical help immediately. This product may interfere with the absorption of other medications. To avoid this, take it at least two hours apart from other medications. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is close to the time of your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Store this medication as directed on the product label. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. Some products may contain inactive ingredients, such as sugar or aspartame, which could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Use caution if you have diabetes, phenylketonuria (PKU), or other conditions requiring dietary restrictions. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, but it is generally considered safe during breastfeeding. Lifestyle changes, such as regular exercise, drinking adequate water, and consuming a fiber-rich diet with foods like bran, fresh fruits, and vegetables, may help prevent or relieve constipation. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms like passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
